lane: LOW audit findings 3 & 4 — the spawner-aura `alpha:` census (towerCover.test.ts) and the pentagram's `--dark-bg` description (check-atlas-scenery.mjs / package.json)
summary: Both findings are REAL and both are still live in the tree at 7d1514b. Neither is a gameplay bug; both are contract/doc defects of exactly the class this project counts as real. FINDING 3: the "aura census" is `src/render/towerCover.test.ts:324-332` — an enumeration test that regex-extracts every `alpha:` property out of `src/render/spawnerZoneRenderer.ts`, pins the count at 6, and requires each expression to END in `* zoneAlpha` or `* bondCover`. Pixi does NOT require `alpha:` (`FillStyle.alpha?: number` with `@default 1`, and `StrokeStyle extends FillStyle`), and this repo is full of `.fill({ color: X })` and `.fill(0xffffff)` written without it — so a seventh draw added in the dominant house idiom keeps the census at 6 and ships a fully-opaque, cover-ignoring layer over a hidden connector, which is the precise eight-session defect the test was written for. It is simultaneously OVER-strict: the capture class `[^,}\n]+` truncates at a comma, so a legitimate `alpha: Math.min(1, x * zoneAlpha)` or a hoisted `const a = 0.3 * zoneAlpha` turns it red. Its own docblock at :242 and :321 claims coverage it does not have, and the two claims disagree with each other by one. FINDING 4: `--dark-bg` is a CLI flag of `scripts/check-atlas-scenery.mjs` (parsed :93) that skips checks 3 and 5, documented at :73 as "the sheet was matted off a DARK background". The pentagram was never matted off anything — `assets-source/pentagram/atlas-specs.json:3` names `build-alpha-sheet-atlas.mjs`, whose header states the sheets arrive RGBA with the cut-out already in the alpha and that "There is no background colour here; keying one would eat the art's own dark ink". The three sibling sheets from that identical intake run in the same `package.json` line WITHOUT the flag, which is the control arm proving the intake does not need it. The two runtime skip lines (:443, :460) therefore print a factually false sentence to the console, the canon documents the exemption only for `lightning-hub` (SPARK_CANON.md:597), and two runbooks — one of them a production source file — tell the next tower author to put every new tower in the "dark-bg group".

findings.claim: The 'aura census' from the handoff is the spawner-zone alpha enumeration in towerCover.test.ts. It regex-extracts every `alpha:` property from spawnerZoneRenderer.ts, pins the total at 6, and requires each captured expression to end in a cover multiplier.

Pixi does NOT require an `alpha:` property on a fill or a stroke. It is optional and defaults to 1 (fully opaque), and StrokeStyle inherits the same optional field — so a draw call written without it is valid TypeScript, valid Pixi, and fully opaque.

Omitting `alpha:` is the DOMINANT idiom in this very repo's renderers, so the omission is the likely form of a future addition, not an exotic edge case. Both the object form without alpha and the bare-colour shorthand are in production files.

findings.claim: CONSEQUENCE — the census is UNDER-strict: a seventh draw added to spawnerZoneRenderer as `.fill({ color: tint })` (no alpha key) leaves the count at 6 and the loop with nothing new to check, so the test stays GREEN while a fully-opaque copy of a connector is redrawn over a tower that structureRenderer has faded to nothing. That is the identical failure mode the file's own docblock says it exists to prevent.

findings.claim: The guard's docblock makes a claim it cannot keep, and the two statements of it disagree by one. :242 says a SIXTH un-scaled fill fails — but six alphas already exist and pass. :321 says a SEVENTH draw added without one turns it red — but only if that draw happens to carry an `alpha:` key.

findings.claim: The census is ALSO over-strict, so it fails correct changes. The capture class `[^,}\n]+` stops at the first comma, so a legitimate clamp `alpha: Math.min(1, 0.4 * zoneAlpha)` is captured as `Math.min(1` and fails the `/\*\s*(zoneAlpha|bondCover)$/` match; hoisting the product into a local (`const a = 0.3 * zoneAlpha; ... alpha: a`) fails for the same reason, as does the equally-correct `alpha: zoneAlpha * 0.5`.

A third hole in the same guard: it pins the TEXT of the multiplier but not that it is the RIGHT cover for that geometry. A per-bond stroke scaled by `zoneAlpha` instead of `bondCover` passes the regex, and would fade with the anchor rather than with the connector it draws.
findings.evidence: .stroke({ width: 1.5 + shimmer * 1.5, color: tint, alpha: bondAlpha * bondCover });

findings.claim: All six current alphas are genuinely cover-scaled, so the production code is CORRECT today — the defect is in the guard's reach, not in the renderer. Nothing else in the file carries opacity (no `.alpha =`, no tint-based fade, no filters), so today the census does enumerate every layer.

fix_shape:
Two independent, test-and-doc-only edits. Neither touches the sim, the wire, or any renderer's behaviour.

FINDING 3 — `src/render/towerCover.test.ts`, the one `it()` at :324-332 plus its two docblocks (:241-244, :318-323). Replace the `alpha:`-property census with a DRAW-CALL census, which is the S182 footer pattern the docblock already cites but does not implement: enumerate `.fill(` + `.stroke(` occurrences in `codeOf('spawnerZoneRenderer.ts')`, pin the total at 6, and require each call's options object to carry a cover-scaled alpha — so a draw added WITHOUT an `alpha:` fails on the count instead of passing invisibly. Two cheap hardenings in the same edit: (a) loosen the value assertion from "must END with `* zoneAlpha|bondCover`" to "must CONTAIN `zoneAlpha` or `bondCover`", and widen the capture past commas (balanced to the closing brace, or capture the whole options object), so a clamp or a hoisted local is not a false red; (b) add a CONTROL arm asserting the bare-colour shorthand `.fill(0x` does not appear in the file, since that form can never carry an alpha key at all. ~25-35 lines in ONE test file, zero production files.

FINDING 4 — a rename + a doc correction. There is no behaviour to change unless the owner wants one. (1) Rename the flag to what it does — `--no-white-checks` (or add it as the true name and keep `--dark-bg` as a deprecated alias for the lightning-hub call) in `scripts/check-atlas-scenery.mjs:73, 93` and rewrite the two printed skip lines at :443 and :460 so they stop asserting a matte that does not exist. (2) Correct `package.json:28`'s pentagram segment to the new flag, and record the pentagram's real justification and its measured numbers at the call site — the project's established answer for exactly this ("naming the exemption at the call site", :89). (3) Fix the two runbook rows that will otherwise repeat it: `src/render/structureRamp.ts:29` and `DAMAGE_RAMP_ADDING_A_TOWER.md:20` — the three sibling towers prove the default for an alpha-matted sheet is NO exemption. (4) Add the pentagram row to `SPARK_CANON.md:597`'s table, or retitle that section so it covers both call sites. ~6 files, ~30 lines, almost all prose.

⚠ One thing I could NOT determine read-only and did not assume: whether the pentagram actually FAILS checks 3/5 without the flag. Running it (`node scripts/check-atlas-scenery.mjs --no-size public/art/pentagram`, needs numpy/scipy/Pillow) is the five-minute measurement that decides whether step (2) records a clean pass — in which case the flag and the 1500 both simply come off — or a real near-white score that then needs the owner. The atlas-specs note describes a "pink glow ring" as the nearest artwork, which is the plausible source of a near-white/scenery score.
four_sites_risk: NONE. Neither fix touches factory/serialize/hash/worker, `PROTOCOL_VERSION` (47), or anything the sim reads. Finding 3 is confined to one `.test.ts`; Finding 4 to a Node script's argv parsing and console strings, `package.json`'s `check:atlas` script, two docblocks and the canon. No `world` field, no wire field, no cadence, no `Math.random`, no wall clock. The only CI-visible surface is the `atlas-guard` job in `e2e.yml:238-241`, which invokes `npm run check:atlas` — so a flag rename must land in `package.json` and the script in the SAME commit or that job goes red (and per the project's own standing rule it reddens CI without blocking the Pages deploy, which is the intended behaviour).
tests_owed:
FINDING 3 — the replacement census IS the test; it owes a captured RED before it is believed, which is this project's own S184 lesson. Mutation-check it both ways: (a) temporarily add `g.circle(cx, cy, 4).fill({ color: 0xffffff });` to `spawnerZoneRenderer.ts` and require the new test to FAIL (the current one passes — that is the whole finding); (b) temporarily rewrite one existing alpha as `alpha: Math.min(1, 0.85 * zoneAlpha)` and require the new test to PASS (the current one fails — the over-strict arm). Restore both byte-identical. No other suite is affected; `spawnerZoneRenderer.ts` is untouched.

FINDING 4 — a source-text assertion is owed precisely because nothing pins these flags today: add to an existing `ci.*.test.ts` a check that every directory in the `check:atlas` script whose atlas-specs names `build-alpha-sheet-atlas.mjs` either runs WITHOUT the white-check exemption or is named in an explicit, commented waiver list. That turns the next silent exemption red. ⚠ CRLF-normalise on read (`.replace(/\r\n/g,'\n')`) — the repo has been bitten by Windows-only false reds in exactly this kind of test. Beyond that, the gate to re-run is `npm run check:atlas` with a CAPTURED `$?`, never through a pipe and never trusting the wrapper's `[exited with code 0]`.
owner_questions: Only if the measurement comes back dirty: if `public/art/pentagram` genuinely scores near-white pockets or scenery once the exemption is removed, do you want the sheet re-rolled (your art budget), or a NAMED, DATED waiver recorded with its measured numbers the way the five size-mismatched sheets already are?
size_estimate:
Micro for each, Micro-to-Standard combined (~8-12K tokens, 7 files, ~60 lines, of which roughly two thirds is prose). Reason: both are fully localised — one test file for Finding 3; a Node script's flag string, one `package.json` line, two runbook rows and one canon table for Finding 4 — with no production behaviour, no wire and no sim in either. The only thing that could push it past Micro is if the pentagram measurement comes back dirty, which turns Finding 4 from a rename into an art decision that is the owner's, not a session's.

VERDICT ON "worth a session's time": NEITHER deserves a session of its own, and BOTH deserve to be ridden along. Finding 3 is the one with real teeth — the guard is the single thing standing between a future renderer edit and a repeat of the defect that survived eight sessions and that the owner personally kept reporting, and it currently cannot see the most idiomatic form of that edit. Ride it into the next session that opens `src/render/` at all (the connector-hiding work for the stink tower and the 12 race/tier-9 towers, item 2 on his list, touches exactly this area). Finding 4 is smaller but is the merge-owner-fix class named in CLAUDE.md §5: a doc/contract correction that is faster and safer done once, in place, than round-tripped — and it has a propagation vector (a production docblock telling the next tower author to repeat it), so leaving it listed costs more than fixing it. Do it as a rider on any session that touches the atlas pipeline or adds tower six; do NOT open a session for it alone.
